title: Allocator thermostat and KV-slot stabilizer to stop cross-tenant OOM cascades
creator: Amelia Park
description: Summary: Multiple customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated and Private environments exposed a common failure mode: rapid memory fragmentation and KV-index tombstone accumulation under bursty inference workloads. This produced tenant-local GPU OOMs and cascading session failures. Root cause appears to be allocator hysteresis + KV-slot allocation race that prevents timely compaction when short-lived sessions spike. This ticket implements an "allocator thermostat" to proactively throttle allocation sources and a "KV-slot stabilizer" that batches tombstone reconciliation to avoid long-tail allocator fragmentation and unsafe parallel compaction.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replay production-like traffic with high small-session churn (prefix-heavy chat workloads) using the incident prompt set
2) Enable stress flags: --kv-prefetch=on --session-evict-delay=0.5s and run 1000 concurrent short sessions targeting hosted pool
3) Observe fragmentation ratio metric > 0.78, KV tombstone growth > 100k, and GPU memory OOMs on node group after ~12 minutes
4) Reproduce on Dedicated cluster with same traffic and lower GPU headroom to confirm cross-env failure mode
root_cause_analysis: Allocator hysteresis: the slab allocator delays reclaim until fragmentation crosses a high-water mark; under bursty churn this allows many small freed segments to remain unusable leading to headroom exhaustion.

KV-slot allocation race: tombstones and index rebuilds run opportunistically on eviction; simultaneous high-velocity evictions cause KV index pointers to be left in inconsistent transient states causing logical leaks (slots marked unavailable but not reclaimed).

Background compaction contention: compaction tasks ran on request threads with high IO priority, amplifying latencies and preventing graceful eviction; on Dedicated this manifested as GPU memory starvation and OOM kills.

Cross-tenant amplification: hosted burst traffic from a single tenant could push a node into a fragmentation state where other tenants were affected due to shared allocator arenas and global prefetch heuristics.
mitigation_playbook: Immediate (hotfix/triage): throttle high-churn tenants by applying request-level rate limiters and enable conservative eviction policy for vulnerable pools (applied 2026-02-16).

Short-term (1 week): deploy runtime-1.116 hotpatch that adds aggressive KV tombstone compaction on low-priority background threads and a pod-level memory headroom guard that evicts oldest sessions first.

This ticket (medium-term): implement allocator thermostat + KV-slot stabilizer with safe concurrency primitives and metrics-driven thresholds; include tenant quarantine mechanism when fragmentation metric breaches emergency threshold.
Monitoring: create composite alert: (fragmentation_ratio > 0.7 && kv_tombstone_rate > 5000/min) -> severity P0 paging and automated tenant throttling.
Customer communication: send postmortem + mitigation steps to affected customers; schedule dedicated follow-ups for Private deployments to support air-gapped upgrades.
design_decisions: Thermostat approach chosen over full allocator rewrite to minimize surface area and enable fast rollback: it injects backpressure into high-allocation call paths and triggers timed compaction cycles when pressure persists.
KV-slot stabilizer will use a batched reconciliation queue with idempotent tombstone application to avoid pointer races; reconcile windows are time-bound to prevent long GC pauses.
Prefer cooperative low-priority background threads for compaction to avoid stealing cycles from inference threads; use tunable quantum sizes for compact passes.
implementation_notes: Add new metrics: allocator_thermostat_engaged_count, allocator_fragmentation_ratio, kv_slot_reconcile_latency, kv_tombstone_compacted_count.
Ensure cross-platform compatibility: behavior should be consistent on GKE-hosted clusters and on-prem Private nodes; avoid kernel-level dependencies.
qa_and_canary_plan: Unit tests for allocator hysteresis and thermostat gating (simulated allocation sequences).
Integration test harness that replays the incident workload and asserts fragmentation_ratio falls below 0.5 after 10 minutes.
Canary rollout: 2% of hosted traffic -> 10% -> 50% over 24h observing OOM rate, tail latency, and kv_reconcile_latency.
Dedicated and Private: staged rollout to a single dedicated pool then to private customer lab environments with support engineers on-call for the first 48h.
deployment_plan: Build runtime-1.118 candidate with feature flags default-off for thermostat and stabilizer.
Smoke deploy to internal perf cluster and run automated load tests for 6 hours.
Canary to hosted region us-west-2 at 2% traffic with health watchers and auto-rollback if OOMs or tail-latency regress by >15%.
Gradual expansion to dedicated pools with manual opt-in per-customer for private installs.
rollback_plan: Clear feature flags and revert to runtime-1.116 snapshot; if revert fails, isolate affected nodes via pool drain and re-create nodes from known-good AMI.
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboards: Memory Resilience overview, per-pool fragment heatmap, KV tombstone trend.
Alerts: fragmentation_ratio > 0.75 sustained 10m -> P0; kv_tombstone_growth > 10k/15m -> P1.
SLA considerations: update incident runbook to include tenant_quarantine and customer notification templates for high-impact events.
post_release_followups: Run 72h soak after 100% rollout and collect broken-down cost delta (token-level and infra) attributed to compaction overhead.
Schedule a retro with SRE, Runtime, and Support teams to validate playbook effectiveness and update escalation thresholds.
Plan longer-term allocator refactor roadmap item if thermostat is repeatedly engaged in >5% of nodes.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary run demonstrates sustained OOM rate reduction >= 80% for the incident workload.
2) Fragmentation_ratio metric consistently stays below 0.55 under same replay within 15 minutes.
3) KV tombstone growth rate reduced by >= 90% during high-churn periods without increasing median inference latency by >5%.
4) All new metrics instrumented and dashboards created; runbooks updated.
